relevance_note: Family report of four TNFAIP3 variant carriers: "A heterozygous c.1727dupC variant in the TNFAIP3 gene (NM_006290) ... was identified in the Pt1 and her mother (Pt 4)" and "also present in the two sisters, Pt2 and Pt3".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; values were typed into a Python builder script in the scratch directory and every span was checked verbatim against the Markdown by script. Table 1 has one row per (patient, manifestation) with Gender and Age at Onset repeated; spans quote the row segment from the patient label. In scope: Pt1-Pt4 (all carriers) and the father (tested in trio NGS with Pt1, labelled 'father of Pt1'; the paper never states his result explicitly, only that the variant was found in Pt1 and her mother, so no variant row and no features for him). 'Four consanguineous patients (three sisters and their mother)' was read as blood relatives, not parental consanguinity, so consanguinity is 'not reported'. Age at onset 'Early childhood (less than 2 years)' (Table 1, all four patients) has no ISO value because it is an upper bound. Ages in the Patients section were used as age at last evaluation; no age at HA20 diagnosis is given. Recurrent fever excluded for Pt1, Pt2 and Pt4 from the named statement 'Only Pt3 presented with recurrent episodes of fevers in childhood.' Counts without names (thyroiditis 3/4, arthritis 2/4, genital ulcers in 1 patient, pSTAT1 increased in 3 of 4) were not used to exclude anyone. Pt3 'no autoimmune manifestation up to the age of 14' was used to exclude the autoimmune checklist items (thyroiditis, type 1 diabetes, autoimmune hepatitis, autoimmune cytopenia); autoantibodies and arthritis left not reported. Anti-TG/anti-TPO values in the 'Autoantibody Positivity' column were recorded as observed anti-thyroid autoantibodies; note Pt4 anti-TG 77 U/ml is below the stated normal value <100 U/ml, while anti-TPO 1016 U/ml is above <40 U/ml. Normal GH secretion tests (Pt2, Pt3) recorded as excluded 'abnormal GH secretion' (D-27); ANA/dsDNA/ENA negative recorded as excluded positive antibodies. Inheritance 'inherited maternal' for Pt2 and Pt3 rests on Pt4 being their stated mother and carrying the same variant (D-24); Pt1's from the trio result. Zygosity for Pt2/Pt3 from the abstract's 'novel heterozygous frameshift mutation (p.His577Alafs*95)'. Functional evidence is from statements about all four patients (Pt1-4 per figure legends); NF-kB phosphorylation only for Pt1 and Pt4; pSTAT1 '3 out of 4' not assigned. Contradictions/discrepancies: Pt3 is '13 year-old' in Patients but Results say 'no autoimmune manifestation up to the age of 14'; Pt2 short stature '3° centile' (text) vs '3°-25° centile' (Table 1); Pt4 adult height '10-20° centile' (text) vs 'Short stature (10-25°)' (Table 1); Pt3 fevers in text started 'between the age of 6 and 8' while Table 1 onset is 'Early childhood (less than 2 years)' for every row. No stacked ' / ' cells in this paper. Variant submitted to ClinVar (SUB10618687) per the paper; not used.
